subject: How does gmultmix() use data from two occasions to model abundance?

messages.author: d640f02d29e7de63
messages.subject: How does gmultmix() use data from two occasions to model abundance?
parts:
Dear Richard and friends,

After dusting off (and attempting to use) some code that Richard kindly helped me develop some time ago, I realize that I don't completely understand what I've been doing with the code.

I've consulted AHM but haven't found an answer to my question, which, simply stated is: "How are the data I collected on two occasions used by gmultmix() to model abundance?"

Here is some background information on my data and model structure:

The survey had two observers who collected data using a dependent double observer method on two occasions. So the y data consist of four columns of counts by the (1) primary observer on the first occasion; (2) secondary observer on the first occasion; (3) primary observer on the second occasion; (4) secondary observer on the second occasion. 

Richard helped develop this piFun for the dependent double observer data:

depDoubleObs <- function(p) { 
  M <- nrow(p) 
  pi <- matrix(NA, M, 2) 
  pi[,1] <- p[,1] 
  pi[,2] <- p[,2]*(1-p[,1]) 
  return(pi) 
} 

And Richard also helped develop this obsToY function, to account for the two occasions:

obsToY <- matrix(1, 2, 2) 
numPrimary <- 2 
obsToY <- kronecker(diag(numPrimary), obsToY) 

I'm using gmultmix to model predicted abundance as a function of site covariates (no observation covariates). Here's one of my models:

m1<-gmultmix(~Area+Habitat+Disturbance,~1,~1,data=umfGMM_BUFF_DIST_0090,mixture="NB") #model abundance as a function of site covariates while accounting for detectability

I understand that the double observer data are used to estimate and account for detectability in the abundance estimates, but how are the data from two occasions used to model abundance? Does the model compute mean abundance across the two occasions, or what?

Many thanks for any help you can provide.

Mark B.
